what_happened: After handoff, the ego drifted left of the recorded path into the lane behind the slower car 56. Although the route command was RIGHT, it kept speeding up to about 6.3 m/s while the gap shrank from 10.9 m to 4.3 m, and its front hit car 56 at 9.2 s. Car 56 was smeared in the camera view but still clearly showed as a vehicle ahead.

The ego had moved about a lane to the left of the recorded path, even though the command was RIGHT. It then kept going at about 7.5 m/s and hit vehicle 87 ahead in its lane: the gap shrank from 11.5 m to 4.6 m and ended in a front collision at 9.6 s, with no slowing at all. The camera view was heavily smeared because the ego was off the recorded path, but the lead car could still be seen. An earlier rear contact happened before 7.6 s and did not cause this front impact.

The route said RIGHT, but the ego drove straight or slightly left, off the recorded path, into the lane behind actor 56. It then closed the gap from about 10.6 m to contact while barely slowing (6.7 to 6.0 m/s) and hit 56 with its front at 9.2s. Actor 13 also hit the ego's rear after the ego left its path; the camera view of the lead car was heavily smeared but still visible.

Although the route command was RIGHT, the ego veered left out of its lane on a busy multi-lane road. With actor 13 only 1–1.7 m ahead and to its right, the ego made front contact with it around 7.2 s, then kept closing on actor 56 in the new lane. Actor 61 hit the ego's rear later; that is secondary because the front collision came first.

The ego had moved about 3–4 m into the lane left of the recorded path. It held about 7.6 m/s while the slower car ahead in that lane (actor 87) closed from 10.3 m to 3.4 m, and the ego hit its rear with its front at 9.6 s. That car looks smeared in the camera because the ego was off the recorded path, but it was still visible, so the policy should have braked. An earlier rear contact on the ego came before this crash and did not cause it.

The route command was RIGHT, but the ego drifted about 4 m left of the recorded path into the next lane and drove in it behind slower vehicle 87. It held about 7.5 m/s and never braked while the gap fell from 11 m to 4 m, then hit 87's rear with its front. Something had already struck the ego's rear before 7.6 s, and the camera showed 87 as a smeared blob, but 87 was clearly visible and closing the whole time.
